title: Fee plan changes, Brent futures stay high
part1:
If this news were a play, the fee plan would change the script halfway through. Brent futures would take center stage as their prices moved. So, how did the story happen?

Trump first posted that he wanted a 20% fee on all cargo passing through the Strait of Hormuz. The plan was meant to help pay for the costs the United States spends to keep the strait safe. The fee had not actually started yet.

But the next day, the story changed suddenly. Trump posted that he would replace the fee with trade and investment deals between Gulf countries and the United States. He said this followed “very productive talks” with Middle Eastern leaders.
part2:
So, what happened to Brent futures? After the change was announced, they briefly lost some of their gains. But they soon returned to a high level, close to where they were before the announcement. When the article was published, they were up about 2.6%, above $85 a barrel.

“We changed the fee plan, so prices should settle down too.” It is easy to expect that ending. But another worry remained on the news stage: possible attacks by the United States and Iran, a blockade at sea, and the safety of tankers. Still, this information alone does not tell us how much these worries changed prices after the announcement.
part3: In other words, the fee plan has a new costume. Brent futures first lost some gains and then recovered. The worries that remain are also on the same stage. It seems a little early to look at only one thing and say, “That settles it.” Even though this is a story about a distant strait, it makes us ask: If the announcement’s script has changed, will the worries leave the stage too?
in_one_line: Trump replaced his proposed Strait of Hormuz fee with trade deals, but Brent oil futures soon returned to high levels.
